facts.fact: The page states that a verified Google Business Profile pulls in around 50 monthly calls on average, with no named source given.
facts.quote: On average, a verified Google Business Profile pulls in around 50 monthly calls.

facts.fact: The page claims that businesses that fully complete their Google Business Profiles see 12% more calls than those with sparse listings, with no named source given.
facts.quote: businesses that take the time to fully complete their profiles see 12% more calls than those with sparse listings.

facts.fact: The page claims that optimized Google Business Profiles show up in 80% more searches, with no named source given.
facts.quote: these optimized profiles show up in 80% more searches

facts.fact: The page states that the Google Business Profile business description allows 750 characters.
facts.quote: You get 750 characters for your business description.

facts.fact: According to the article, 77% of consumers say they 'always' or 'regularly' check reviews when looking for a local business; the source of this statistic is not named in the chunk.
facts.quote: In fact, **77% of consumers** say they 'always' or 'regularly' check reviews when looking for a local business.

facts.fact: The article advises that a business's Name, Address, and Phone number (NAP) across the web should be 100% identical, with the same spelling and abbreviations.
facts.quote: Your NAP needs to be **100% identical** across the web. Same spelling, same abbreviations, same everything.

facts.fact: Google Posts can include a "Call Now" button, which the article describes as a non-negotiable feature for businesses trying to drive more calls.
facts.quote: this feature is a non-negotiable because you can add a **"Call Now" button** right on the post.

facts.fact: The article recommends that a business seed its Q&A section by listing the top 3-5 questions it receives on the phone and answering them as the owner.
facts.quote: Jot down the top 3-5 questions you get on the phone all day long.

facts.fact: Adwave's example offer for a homeowner's Google Post is a $99 Spring HVAC Tune-Up Special, used as an illustration rather than a stated price.
Adwave says that if its dashboard shows ads hitting their stride between 6 PM and 9 PM on weeknights, the business should staff up to answer calls; this is a hypothetical example.
facts.quote: If your Adwave dashboard shows that your ads are hitting their stride between **6 PM** and **9 PM** on weeknights

facts.fact: Adwave states that a unique phone number used only on a Google Business Profile lets the business know with 100% certainty that a call came from the profile.
facts.quote: You'll know with **100% certainty** that a call came from your profile

facts.fact: Adwave recommends running a profile A/B test for at least two weeks, and preferably about four weeks, before comparing call volume.
facts.quote: Let it run for a few weeks (at least two, maybe four)

facts.fact: Adwave recommends adding a new Google Post or a fresh batch of photos to a Google Business Profile once a week.
facts.quote: Aiming to add a new Google Post or a fresh batch of photos **once a week**
